stem:
A 26-year-old Rh-negative woman delivers an Rh-positive infant without incident. During her second pregnancy, again with an Rh-positive fetus, the fetus develops severe anemia.

The fetal hemolysis is caused by maternal antibody of which of the following classes crossing the placenta?

options.label: A
options.misconception: The isohemagglutinin class is being assumed to cross the placenta.
options.explanation: IgM (the class of ABO isohemagglutinins) cannot cross the placenta; only IgG reaches the fetus, which is why ABO incompatibility is milder than Rh disease.

options.label: B
options.misconception: A mucosal antibody is being credited with placental transfer.
options.explanation: IgA predominates at mucosal surfaces and in secretions; it does not cross the placenta and plays no role in hemolytic disease of the newborn.

options.label: C
options.misconception: The allergy antibody is being linked to fetal hemolysis.
options.explanation: IgE mediates allergic and antiparasitic responses and does not cross the placenta; the transplacental hemolytic antibody is IgG.

options.label: D
options.misconception: A B-cell surface receptor is being treated as a secreted effector.
options.explanation: IgD functions mainly as a B-cell receptor and is not transferred across the placenta; maternal anti-Rh IgG is the hemolytic agent.

options.label: E
options.misconception: None; IgG is the only antibody class that crosses the placenta.
options.explanation: Anti-Rh IgG antibodies formed during the first pregnancy persist in the mother; IgG is the only class of antibody that can cross the placenta, so in a second Rh-positive pregnancy these antibodies attach to fetal Rh-positive erythrocytes and hemolyze them.

context: Learning objective: explain hemolytic disease of the newborn. An Rh-negative mother exposed to Rh-positive fetal cells produces anti-Rh IgG. Because IgG is the only antibody class that crosses the placenta, a subsequent Rh-positive fetus is attacked in utero; Rho(D) immune globulin prevents the primary response.
imageCaption: Bilirubin: spleen Hb breakdown -> unconjugated (albumin) -> hepatic conjugation -> bile -> gut bacteria -> urobilinogen/stercobilin; some urobilinogen -> urine.
